intro: Ghost Archipelago is a related but separate Osprey ruleset — a Heritor (caster) and Warden (nature-magic specialist) lead a Crew across a chain of islands instead of a Wizard leading a Warband — so nearly everything below is structurally new relative to the Frostgrave rulebook, even where the mechanics closely parallel it. A few stat-block values could not be confirmed and are marked with "?".

sections.title: New core mechanics
sections.blurb: Turn order is Heritor phase → Warden phase → Crew phase → Creature phase (3-step AI: fight if engaged, shoot/close on the nearest visible foe, else random move). Combat/shooting math mirrors core Frostgrave closely (Fight/Shoot rolls, cover, push-back), with an optional Critical Hit rule (natural 20 auto-wins and doubles damage) and an optional Wounded rule (≤4 Health = 1 action & -2 to all rolls).

entries.name: Crew composition
entries.text: Max 10: 1 Heritor + 1 Warden (mandatory, only one ever per crew) + up to 8 crewmen (max 4 paid Specialists). All rolls use d20.

entries.name: Building a Heritor
entries.text: Picks 5 of 30 shared Abilities (one at Utilization Number 3, four at UN5); may raise one non-Armour stat by +1; 5 item slots.

entries.name: Utilization Rolls & Blood Burn (signature new subsystem)
entries.text: Using a Heritor Ability costs 1 self-damage ("Blood Burn") to attempt, +2 more on a failed d20-vs-UN roll. Extra attempts the same turn stack a penalty to the UN: +0/+3/+6/+9/+12/+15 for the 1st–6th attempt — a practical cap of ~6/turn.

entries.name: Building a Warden
entries.text: Base M6 F+1 S+0 A10 W+4 H14; picks a Branch (below); learns 4 starting spells (3 in-Branch, 1 out-of-Branch at +4 Casting Number); 3 item slots; can never wear armour or a shield.

entries.name: Split Stats
entries.text: Notation like "+2/+3": first number is the true/base stat for leveling, second is the current effective stat for rolls.

entries.name: Empowering & resisting spells
entries.text: A Warden can empower a cast (or her own resistance roll) by trading Health 1-for-1, even to the point of a killing cast. Targets resist vs. the higher of the final Casting Roll or 14.

entries.name: Swimming Rolls
entries.text: Activating in deep water needs a Will roll (TN5, modified by armour/shield/treasure); fail = no activation + damage. Amphibious/Aquatic traits bypass it entirely.

entries.name: Small Boats
entries.text: Capacity 6, moves 2"+1"/rider (max 6"), -1 Fight/Shoot aboard, boarding needs a Fight roll; can be attacked (Fight+0/Armour14/Health30).

entries.name: Map Stones (campaign win condition)
entries.text: 10 unique, unsellable clue-items toward the legendary Crystal Pool; +20 XP each; collecting all 10 is the stated campaign endgame.

entries.name: New Recruits
entries.text: If only the Heritor dies, the Warden's level sets the replacement (capped gains); if only the Warden dies, it's the Heritor's level ÷3. Both dying disbands the crew.

sections.title: Treasure
sections.blurb: Treasure Table results run gold → Herb/Potion → Weapon/Armour → Magic Item → Map Stone as the roll climbs (1–22, with +2 possible for central treasure). Plus a full Weapons & Armour enchantment table (Superior/Magic variants of every weapon class, a Bright Shield, three tiers of Magic Light Armour, a Ring of Protection) and 10 unique, unsellable Map Stones (Arkliss, Breenlin, Cortavious, Dyrenten, Eccorient, Foqueth, Gaelbys, Huventh, Indruline, Jancis) driving the campaign's endgame.

sections.title: Ships & campaign systems
sections.blurb: Injury/Death: crewmen roll d20 (1–4 dead / 5–8 miss a game / 9+ fine); Heritor/Warden use a dedicated Survival Table plus a 10-entry Permanent Injury Table (split-stat penalties). Experience: Heritor and Warden level up on fully separate tracks (100 XP/level each), each choosing between a stat increase, a lower Utilization/Casting Number, or a new ability/spell (gated to roughly one new one per 4–5 levels). Buying items requires a d20 12+ availability roll at 2× sell price, once per item per mainland trip (200gc round trip, 175gc with Swift Sails).

sections.title: Traps in Ghost Archipelago (Spellcaster Issue 2)
sections.blurb: Mirrors the Frostgrave trap rules (Into the Breeding Pits) for Ghost Archipelago. A natural 1 on initiative springs a trap: that player picks the target (any figure, including uncontrolled creatures) and rolls the Trap List; effects resolve immediately, before other actions. Optional "Treasure Traps": a Random Encounter roll of 1 while picking up treasure means it was trapped.

sections.title: Frostgrave Mech War (Spellcaster Issue 2)
sections.blurb: A generic mech-vs-mech variant reusing the core engine. Alternate activating one mech at a time until one side is exhausted, then the other side activates all that remain. "Health" is renamed "Structure." A mech may fire multiple weapons in one shoot action, but each weapon fired that turn adds a cumulative -1 to all its shooting rolls that turn. For every full 5 points of damage from a single attack, the mech suffers one Critical Hit (stacking).

rows.text: Engine Damage: -1 Move
Servo Damage: -1 Fight
Targeting Glitch: -1 Shoot / -1 Armour
Cracked Armour: +5 Structure damage
Internal Explosion: random weapon destroyed
Weapon Hit: mech destroyed
Reactor Hit: pilot killed, mech destroyed
Cockpit Hit: mech destroyed

sections.title: Ulterior Motives in Ghost Archipelago (Spellcaster Issue 3)
sections.blurb: Ports the Frostgrave "Ulterior Motives" card system to Ghost Archipelago. Each player secretly draws one card after table edges are set but before deployment; cards specify optional Red Herring terrain/creatures to disguise the true objective. Common terrain: Arcane Disk, Gateway, Pit, Runic Stone, Sarcophagus, Statue, Trap Door, Zombie.

entries.name: The Broken Map

entries.name: The Ancestral Gate

entries.name: Death Do Us Part

entries.name: The Boundary Stone

entries.name: The Forgotten Saint
entries.text: Pledge gold at a statue for a chance to heal an injury or gain XP.

sections.title: High-Level Heritors (Spellcaster Issue 5)
sections.blurb: Blood Burn still costs Health per power attempt and still damages on failure, but the damage shrinks (never to zero) as the Heritor levels. Specialist Crew caps at 4 early on, rising to 8 of 8 crew by level 40. Legendary Crew unlock at Heritor level 10, occupying a specialist slot each (a level-10 Heritor could run 5 specialists, or 1 Legendary + 4 specialists). Building a High-Level Heritor: pick a level (= total advancements) → take advancements one at a time → roll the Treasure Table once per level (reroll Map Stones) → recruit a Warden at level ÷ 3 (round up), who takes one advancement per level → hire crew up to the table's limits → distribute the accumulated treasure. Hiring Legendary Crew requires returning to the mainland; survival uses the Heritor/Warden Survival Table (main rulebook p.59) with "Close Call" treated as "Full Recovery" and "Smashed Jaw" rerolled.

entries.text: A timed geyser eruption lets an adjacent figure bathe a weapon to make it magic (+1 Fight if mundane).

entries.name: Box of Snakes
entries.text: Open a cursed sarcophagus (Fight TN14) to release two large snakes and two special treasure tokens exchangeable for Golden Snake items.

entries.name: The Silver Helm
entries.text: A Will Roll TN14 removes a helmet hidden on a statue, securing a Piscian Helmet.

entries.name: Farsight
entries.text: Reciting a prayer in a gateway (Will TN18) grants bonus XP by which figure succeeds.

entries.name: Bait and Switch
entries.text: Revealing at a trap door swaps the central treasure onto it, wherever it currently is.

entries.name: The Cursed Stone
entries.text: Touching a runic stone punishes enemies with a +5 attack but rewards your own figures with XP and a treasure reroll.

entries.name: The Point of Power
entries.text: A Warden casting spells atop an arcane disk gets +4 to the roll and bonus XP per cast (max +100).

sections.title: Giant Tortoises (Spellcaster Issue 6)
sections.blurb: A full new mount/pack-animal subsystem. After any game, a Heritor may attempt a Will Roll TN20 to find a tribe selling one for 300gc; further tortoises cost 250gc in ship modifications. Don't count against crew limit (max 5 in a crew); activate only alongside an adjacent crew member (once/turn, max 4.5" move); survival rolled as a specialist crewman if killed. As a mount: one action to mount/dismount; follows small-boat rules but moves on land, carries up to 3 riders, may make two move actions/turn (4.5" total); never counts as In Combat itself; a rider may attack anyone in base contact with the tortoise without the usual -1 Fight penalty. Carries up to 15 items total (each rider uses 5 capacity); anyone on/adjacent may exchange a carried item. Attacking an unarmoured part costs -2 Shoot/Fight but treats Armour as 12 instead of 16. Never jumps, climbs above ~1", or picks up treasure; may never use items.

rows.text: M 3 · F +0 · Sh — · A 16 · W +3 · H 14 · Notes Animal, Armoured Shell, may serve as mount, carrying capacity 15.

sections.title: Ulterior Motives (Spellcaster Issue 7)
sections.blurb: 16 new cards, bringing the Ghost Archipelago Ulterior Motives set (Issues 3, 5, and 7 combined) to 40 cards — matching the original Frostgrave set size.

entries.name: Mercy Re-Killing
entries.text: Killing a zombie lets a crew member recover a necklace worth a ruby (60gc).

entries.name: The Mirror of Antosis
entries.text: Passing through a gateway (Will TN8) splits a figure in two at half Health each, merging again at game end.

entries.name: Rise like the Phoenix
entries.text: Standing on an arcane disk risks possession by a fiery demon, granting combat bonuses and Flying.

entries.name: Sundial
entries.text: Revealing on an arcane disk deals 2 damage to everyone in LoS but grants XP per figure hit.

entries.name: Down the Pit
entries.text: A crew member near a pit can pull out a rescued crewmate (Health 5) on an 11+.

entries.name: Gateway of Nedrezzar
entries.text: Speaking an incantation in a gateway (Will TN16) places a bonus special treasure token.

entries.name: Revenge Served Cold
entries.text: An opponent controls a zombie; XP swings depending on who kills it and when.

entries.name: Summon the Worm
entries.text: A ritual at a pit (Will TN18) summons a giant worm and grants a free map stone.

entries.name: The Golden Skull
entries.text: Opening a sarcophagus (Fight TN14) secures a Golden Skull treasure or an equivalent roll.

entries.name: The Secrets of Life and Death
entries.text: Copying writings at a sarcophagus (Will TN14) grants the Warden +80 XP if secured.

entries.name: Doorway to Neverwhen
entries.text: Opening a trap door (Fight/Will TN16) lets the crew exit the table through it with any carried treasure.

entries.name: The Buried Ship
entries.text: Opening a trap door (Fight TN12) lets figures search for treasure inside over several turns.

entries.name: Statue of the Troll
entries.text: Speaking words of power (Will TN16) can animate a statue into an Island Troll that may join the crew.

entries.name: Stone of Lost Knowledge
entries.text: A Warden who succeeds a Will Roll (TN14) may, after the game, forgo XP earned to instead immediately gain a level and a new spell of choice (may temporarily exceed the normal spell cap for their level; no further new spells until legal again). Red Herrings: Swamp Zombie, Sarcophagus.

entries.name: The Siren in Stone
entries.text: A singing statue (Will TN16) heals or incapacitates everyone within 12" by their own Will roll.

entries.name: The Rite of Fire
entries.text: The Heritor may challenge a runic stone (immediate +5 attack) for a permanent Fight bonus and XP.
